237. The section (M. Oliva) reconstructs the situation of the service part of the house, accessible from the entrance at no. 1, around the atrium (C) and the courtyard (N), with the painted lararium under the slope of the S portico, the kitchen covered by a small flat canopy and the rooms on the upper floor; on the back wall of (N) is the painted electoral inscription.

238. Courtyard (N): the bottom of the small impluvium of cocciopesto is adorned with a motif outlined in small, widely spaced white tesserae, datable to the Republican age. In the center there is a circle with knots, at the corners quarter circles.

239. The painted lararium of the courtyard (N) is divided into two bands: at the bottom is the plinth with plants usual on the walls painted in the fourth style; at the top center is an altar (represented as if it were made of Numidian marble), around which a snake wraps its wide coils; next to the sacrificing Genius with cornucopia is a female figure, also sacrificing, identified with Juno, on the sides of the altar the tibicine and the Camillus as well as the Lares. The dimensional ratios are not respected and the most important figures — according to the ways of 'plebeian painting' — are much taller than the others, in particular the 'small' servants of sacrifice. In the center is a tabula ansata without an inscription. 72 AFS D4442
240. The mouth of a fluted travertine cistern in the courtyard (N) dates back to the Republican age. 77 N44465
241. On the masonry counter of the kitchen (?) are placed amphorae bottoms and a mortar. TI N44464
242. The tile with a blowhole above the kitchen counter.

243. The final III style decoration of the S wall of the room (R) was about to be abolished and a layer of plaster had already been laid in the middle area; of the decoration of the previous phase, the remains of a metope frieze and a garland are preserved.
244. Room (R), S wall, section O: a mask of Dionysus hung from the aedicule in the upper area, on the sides there is a low frieze with motifs typical of the final phase of the III style. 77 N44466

245. Room (S) occupies part of the surface of a previous, larger room: the ornamentation of the cocciopesto floor is in fact interrupted by the N wall of the room [corresponding to the S wall of (R) with decoration of the third style being redone, seen in the previous photos]. The center of the floor, executed in the era of the first style, has a medallion with a network of diamonds inscribed within a square with a meandering border on a different scale

246. Room (S), N wall with circular window: the IV style decoration overlaps the simple moulded frame. The plinth is red, adorned with compartments with plants; the yellow panels in the middle area, partly turned red due to the effect of fire, contained vignettes with cupids; upper red area.

247. Room (S), wall E with the door to the compluviated room (O): remains of a fresco of the fourth style, with a red plinth, yellow middle area and red upper area, which partly overlaps the moulded cornice.
248. Room (S), wall $ with decoration of the fourth style partly relocated în situ.

249. Room (S), S wall with square window and splayed window open to the courtyard (N), around which the IV style decoration is arranged, with panels with candelabra and arched garlands in the yellow middle area.

250. Room (U): on the N wall, a reed (partly reconstructed), part of a decoration of the fourth style is preserved. The plinth is black, the middle area has a white central panel and side panels, in which the yellow background has turned red following contact with fire; edges of carpet and compartments.
251. Room (U), wall E with the door open towards (W), which partly occupies the space of the central panel with a white background; Twisted candelabra and Okeanos mask compartment. IV style.
252. Environment (U), detail of fig. Previous: partition with bearded male protome. 77 N44589

253. Room (U): the better state of conservation on the S wall allows the IV style decoration to be evaluated. The black plinth has panels with plants, the middle area has a large white panel framed by candelabra and yellow side panels; the partitions are adorned with male protomes. 77 N44586
254. Room (U), W wall with the window open to the courtyard (N) and remains of a fresco of the IV style. Ti N44587
255. Room (Y) preserves in the centre of the wall O the remains of a decoration with a red middle z0na and a yellow band, later covered with white plaster.
256. Room (Z): this room, located in the service part of the house, also received (in the imperial age?) a floor of cocciopesto adorned with white tiles with a motif of tangent circles. 77 N44584

257. Room (Z): the room bears a decoration of the fourth style of rather reduced quality, as expected given its location in the service part of the house, but retains all the elements of the decorative system: the division between the plinth and the middle area, the scansion in panels, the figurative motifs within medallions and squares, the edges of carpet,  the stucco frame.
258. Detail of fig. previous: the small picture (with illegible ornamentation) in the center of the white middle area. IV style.
259. Detail of fig. 257: in the right panel, within a medallion bordered by a garland (traced with the help of a compass) is a thin rampant panther executed with a very clumsy hand.

260. Room (Z), wall E with decoration of the fourth style: in the red plinth there are panels with plants, in the centre of the white middle area there is an aedicule (?) with a painting, on the right the infill of a window, which has remained unplastered. 77 N44474
261. Room (Z), detail of fig. previous: the central painting with still life, consisting of only three rather spaced elements, at the top a basket, at the bottom a peacock and fruit.
262. Room (Z), S wall with the large window that takes light from the courtyard (N): decoration of the fourth style (red plinth and white middle area with vignettes with birds).
263. Room (Z), W wall with fresco of the fourth style. 77 N44472
264. Detail of fig. previous: the medallion on the left (bordered by a garland traced with the help of a compass) perhaps contained a griffin.
265. Detail of fig. 263: rampant antelope in the right panel.  77 N44476

266. Remains of decoration of the third style on the N wall of room {5} on the upper floor: black geometric plinth, white band adorned with drops and lotus buds, the base of the red panel of the middle area.
267. Room {5} on the upper floor, wall E: remains of III style decoration with a black geometric plinth.
268. Room {5}, wall O: also on this wall, only the black geometric plinth of the room on the second floor is preserved. III style.
269. Fragment of a wall painted in the third style in the room on the second floor {6}: the middle area has a pink panel, the upper area has a black panel. 77 N44661

270. Another lararium (here in a watercolour by M. Oliva, 1977) has come to light in a garden to the north of the House of Polybius: the small niche — in which a lamp was placed — is surrounded by garlands and towards it are oriented the two large agathodemon serpents that structure the decoration: above their coils are in fact represented the Lares,  while within the field defined by them are the Genius between two female figures (in the center), Bacchus with thyrsus and jug and Mercury with bag and caduceus (on the right), a pair of peasants (? on the left), and at the bottom two palm trees.

1. Façade corresponding to numbers 4 and 6, with a high red plinth, middle and upper area of fake opus quadratum and with paintings of Aeneas, Anchises and Ascanius, and of Romulus with trophy, on the sides of entrance 5. The electoral inscription for A. Vettium Firmum allows the paintings to be dated to before 72 AD, the year in which he ran for aedile.

2. Façade of number 5, section O: detail of the panel on a white background with the representation of Romulus wearing a golden breastplate and a short cloak on a red tunic, carrying a sword on the left side, holding a spear in his right hand and on his left shoulder a trophy of weapons consisting of cuirass, shield and helmet, mounted on a gnarled staff. Advance to the right, looking backwards.

3. Façade of number 5, section E: detail of the panel on a white background with Aeneas, whose clothing corresponds to that of Romulus in the previous figure, who advances to the left looking backwards, and carries his elderly father on his shoulders, wrapped in a dark red cloak, holding a box in his hands. Aeneas holds in his right hand the hand of the little Ascanius who wears a cloak on his short tunic raised and wavy by the rapid gait, and on his head a Phrygian cap, while in his right hand he clutches a pedum. It is clear the painter's intent to underline the link between the two semi-divine heroes dressed in the same way, walking in the same way even if in a symmetrical position, to claim the link between Rome and Troy evoked in Virgil's poem.   AFS C640
4. Façade of number 5, with a red plinth with electoral inscriptions including that of Fabius Ululitremulus who, with Sula, supports C. Cuspio Pansa and L. Popidius Secundus.
1. Façade in opus incerta with jambs and vertical chains in opus quadrata of parallelepiped blocks of Sarno limestone. The lintel and window jambs are also made of limestone blocks.

2. Vestibule (A): the monolithic limestone threshold has on the outside the recesses for the wooden door jambs and, on the inside, the square recesses for the bronze gangs that were found in situ, and the smaller ones for the ups and downs of the leaves of the three-leaf door that had iron handles.
3. Vestibule (A): the floor, sloping considerably towards the atrium, dates back to the first style and is made of papier-mâché with scattered limestone flakes.
4. Vestibule (A), wall E: the plinth, the middle and the upper area have a simple rough plaster applied in several stages, as can be identified from the caesura line of the pontate. 79 N50855

5. Vestibule (A), wall O: the large gaps in the plaster allow us to recognize the building technique adopted, an accurate uncertain work of Sarno limestone with sturdy jambs whose parallelepiped blocks fit deeply into the structure.

6. Atrium (B): the environment is dominated by the majestic Corinthian tuff columns, with Attic bases, dating back to the second century BC, which surround the impluvium. On the edge of the latter there is the marble table, the monopodium, fluted, also made of marble, on which the fountain statuette of Satyr was placed, while inside there was the basin into which the gush of water fell. Note the extension of the plastered surfaces in the 30s, the time of the photograph's execution.  AFS C480

7. Atrium (B): the tuff impluvium has the edge with an A2 type molding, with a cyma reversa slightly more flattened than the types of a few decades earlier. In the southern half of the bottom, a cut was made to house a water supply fistula, ending in the center, where a marble disk was placed. The same pipe also fed the statuette of the Satyr who, clutching a wineskin, made the water gush into the basin in front (in the photo there are only the supports, decorated with rosettes). On the bottom you can recognize the tablinum (H). 79 N50899

8. Atrium (B): detail of the papier-mâché floor with scattered white limestone flakes, which forms a single unit with that of the vestibule, but which had been redone in imitation of a previous one preserved in sections S and E.

9. Atrium (B), N wall: in the W section, the lararium aedicule (32) of the first century A.D. was leaning against the masonry in place on the frame, which dates back to the second century B.C. due to the considerable height and tapering of the door of the room (33).

10. Atrium (B), wall N, section E: the door to the room (D) was first narrowed and then completely walled up, leaving în situ the threshold visible below the masonry in opus incerta inserted in the one in situ on the frame. In the last period of the city's life, the rough plaster was laid there, which should almost certainly, due to the social level of the owners, have received a fresco worthy of such an imposing environment, whose height exceeded the 7.20 m of the columns with capitals.
11. Atrium (B), wall E with the entrances of (E) and (F); On the left you can see the more ancient papier-mâché floor, less compact than the redone one.

13. Atrium (B), N-W corner: the lararium aedicule stands on a masonry podium with a small arched deposit. It has the shape of a small temple supported by columns and a small pillar placed against the wall, the roof is sloping with gables, in each of which there is a trace of a white stucco patera. 79 N50848
12. Atrium (B), N-W corner with the door of the room (31) and the lararium aedicule (32) leaning against it.

14. Atrium (B): detail of the panel on the S side of the impluvium with a bardiglio top, supported by small pillars of white marble, podged and ending in a lion's paw that rests on a slate base with marble inlays of contrasting color, resting on a larger cubic base of travertine.
15. Atrium (B): once the rectangular basin of the basin has been removed, the feet remain with moulded bases and rosette in relief, on the short faces.  79 N50891

16. Atrium (B): in the SW section of the room there is the large safe covered with iron sheets, fixed with studs, placed on the masonry base, deformed and broken by the weight of the burial materials. It was found empty and the iron shovel, the lamp and the sandstone whetstone found there had accidentally fallen into it.

17. Cubicle (C), wall E: the splayed and plastered window, belonging to a construction phase of the house prior to that of the last years of life, was walled up when the small cubicle room was transformed into a passage to the triclinium (D). Of the wall covering, only a stretch of rough plaster remains in the upper area.

18. Cubicle (C), S wall: of the II style decoration a section of the upper area with a row of yellow elongated ashlars with purple veins, the molded stucco cornice, the frieze whose size is established by the course of the holes for the grappas of the upper stucco cornice, are preserved; the area above is of rough plaster.
19. Cubicle (C), S wall: detail of the II style section. Below the row of yellow and purple ashlars, you can see the traces of a painted ovoli frame.
20. Triclinium (D), NW corner: only the yellow plinth and the purple plinth of the II style decoration remain, which Sogliano (cited in bibl., p. 252) had seen almost entirely destroyed. 79 N50836

21. Triclinium (D), S wall: the large window, which had a wooden sill, interrupted the decoration which had partly been redone with rough plaster near jamb O. The purple plinth had a yellow podium and a green border and according to Sogliano imitated "with poor execution a long slab of variously colored marble". In the middle area there are red orthostats arranged at the head and green arranged at the edge; above rows of yellow and green ashlars, followed by a cornice supported by corbels and other rows of smaller ashlars imitating polychrome marbles; of the stucco frames above, only the holes of the grappa remained. At the top, the wall was rough because it was probably covered by curtains or tapestries. 79 N50835

22. Triclinium (D), wall O: the fall of the plaster highlighted the masonry structure in situ with a limestone frame on which the decoration of the II style similar to that of the S wall was extended; only that of the E wall differed in the details of the plinth where a fake marble inlay with yellow rhomboidal slabs was painted with green triangles around it.
23. Cubicle (E): the floor is made of travertine with medium-sized flakes.

24. Cubicle (E): the monolithic lava threshold has dovetail recesses for the wooden jambs, circular ones for hinges and square recesses for gangheri, as well as small recesses for the ups and downs of the door leaves.

25. Cubicle (E), N wall: the red plinth is divided into panels, the white middle area has a stylized central gabled aedicule, between panels that have lost the figurative details present in the center due to the poor state of preservation.

26. Cubicle (E), wall E: in the red plinth the squares with corollas of the side panels can be distinguished. In the center of the white middle area, under the aedicule with a low tympanum, you can see the medallion with busts and in the side panels, with square carpet edges, the traces of the vignettes with the eagle clutching a rabbit in its claws. In the upper area you can see the holes for the grappas of the stucco frame.
27. Cubicle (E), wall E, section N: detail of the red plinth with concentric squares containing a small corolla. 79 N53250

28. Cubicle (E), wall E, central section: detail of the aedicule bordered by twisted reeds, of which the engraving of the preparatory drawing can be seen, and with a central medallion (diameter 0.21). Already at the time of the shooting, the two busts on a blue background, interpreted as Mars, characterized by the golden helmet, and Venus, were barely legible; the frame was red, while the outermost garland was green with yellow and red flowers.
29. Cubicle (E), wall E, central section: detail of the upper unplastered area, in which a walled-up window can be recognized.

30. Cubicle (E), S wall: the preservation of the upper part of the middle area makes it possible to identify above the panels a motif of garlands that is connected to the pediment of the central aedicule, resulting in an undulating motif in red on a white background.
31. Cubicle (E), S wall, section O: the non-frontal shot highlights the rough upper area above the stucco frame of which the holes of the grappa can be seen. 79 N53248

32. Cubicle (E), wall O: the continuous section was divided into two panels in which there were vignettes with a flying griffin. In the part above the panels, which here takes on the appearance of a frieze, the garlands end behind a square with a corolla.

33. Cubicle (F), N wall: in the high red plinth, articulated in panels, there are no figurative elements, and in the middle area with a white background small paintings that have completely vanished, already at the time of their discovery in 1905. Above ran a frieze with birds and the molded stucco frame which was followed higher up by another, before the area left to rough plaster.
34. Cubicle (F), N wall, section O: detail of the frieze with a bird to the right, resting on the painted frame. 79 N53257

35. Cubicle (F), wall E in which the paratactic scheme of the panels that follow one another in the plinth and in the middle area is repeated. In the upper area, covered with rough plaster, you can see two closed windows. 79 N53261
36. Cubicle (F), wall E, section N: detail of the frieze with a white background with a peacock advancing to the right.

37. Cubicle (F), wall E: detail of the upper area in which you can see, above the walled window and the rough plaster, the yellow band that was once bordered at the bottom by a stucco frame of which the holes of the grappa remain.

38. Cubicle (F), wall S with the door and window towards the wing (G). The faint traces of the decoration painted on the white background of the middle area allow us to identify a stylized aedicule and a bird, facing left, resting on a horizontal beam, above the door.
39. Cubicle (F), wall W, section N beyond the door to the atrium. Only the upper part of a stylized architectural glimpse crossed by a candelabrum that ends in the frieze remains.

40. Cubicle (F), W wall, section N: detail of the frieze on a white background with the end of the candelabrum, placed under a blue curtain raised above an arch supported by the tails of two dolphins; a garland stretched in large and sparse tufts crosses the frieze.

41. Wing (G), NE corner: the wall is almost completely devoid of the rough plaster that covered the structure in opus incerta, with jambs in opus quadrata. The floor is in papier-mâché with scattered white limestone flakes.
42. Tablinum (H): the cocciopesto floor with dotted with small white limestone tiles dates back to the II style.

43. Tablinum (H): in jamb E were found two bronze studs with representations of a ship's bow with a rostrum and the front of a bull and a ship's bow simpler than the previous one, and without a rostrum, but with a larger forepart of the torus. On the ground there is the upper part of a Corinthian tuff capital. The walls are covered only with the preparatory layer, perhaps waiting for a refined decoration.
44. Cubicle (K), wall N with the recess for the bed at the level of the plinth on a white background, bordered at the top by a clearly visible red band on the wall E.
45. Under the stairs (0) with recesses for the shelves made in the rough plaster of the NE and W walls.

46. Under the stairs (0): in the large plaster gap on the W wall, immediately above the recess for the lower shelf, a fragment of plaster with polychrome braid and one of a moulded stucco frame can be seen as reused materials.  79 N53424
48. Under the stairs (0), wall O: to the left of the hole for the shelf you can read the graffiti Atti.
47. Under the stairs (o), wall W: detail of the N section of the plaster with Saufe Cei graffiti.
50. Under the stairs (0), wall W: in the central section it reads A/fi. 79 N53431
49. Under the stairs (0), wall O: to the right of the same hole as in the previous photo, it reads Coel(1).
51. Under the stairs (o), wall W: again in the central section there is graffiti Valeri.
52. Under the stairs (o), wall O: in the S section there is a sketch of a small house with a door. 79 N53427

53. Oecus(3): the floor in white limestone with polychrome limestone flakes probably dates back to the II style, like the paintings. The threshold towards the peristyle, rather poorly preserved, was made of flakes of white limestone.
54. Oecus (3): the close-up detail of the floor highlights the variety of red, green, yellow, grey-blue limestone flakes used. 79 N53391

55-56. Oecus(3), N wall interrupted by the door to the peristyle. Especially in the E section, the black plinth and the middle area with red orthostats, bordered at the ends by white corner pillars, are preserved.

55-56. Oecus(3), N wall interrupted by the door to the peristyle. Especially in the E section, the black plinth and the middle area with red orthostats, bordered at the ends by white corner pillars, are preserved.

57. Oecus (3), wall E: the beautiful and articulated scenography, preserved almost entirely, belongs to phase IIA of the II style. In fact, the black plinth appears as a continuous counter, with little volume, in front of which are placed male herms, thin metal candelabras and two Sirens. In the middle area, a wall with a red background with lateral avant-corps supported by slender fluted columns whose Attic base rests on the podium of the plinth is interrupted in the center by a door framed by scaled columns. Through the open door you can see a female statue placed in front of an apse protected at the top by a curtain, on the sides of which you can see two colonnades in perspective, emerging against the blue of the sky, beyond the red partitions. Two wooden columns decorated with ashlars and relief figures support the first segment of the corniINS. 14, 4

58. Oecus(3), wall E, section N: the herm placed in the plinth to support the podium is not in correspondence with a load-bearing element of the middle area, unlike the slender metal candelabrum that is located below the wooden column with ashlar drums and reliefs. The thin fluted columns, which support Tuscan-type capitals, are not in axis with each other, although they support the cornice of the lateral avant-corps, and this anomaly stands out more for the absence of the base in the left one, which seems to rest behind the plinth, like the pillar in the concave corner and the ashlar column. However, if considered in the upper part, they determine a sort of aedicule on the sides of the painting with Venus.
59. Oecus(3), E face, N section: detail of the plinth with the male herm.

60. Oecus(3), wall E, section N: detail of the upper part with the painting (0.60 x 0.50, stolen in 1982) depicting Pompeian Venus. The goddess, bejeweled, wears a green mantle on her yellow tunic, holds the long sceptre in her left hand, towards her flies an erote, garlanded, carrying a crown of flowers; he stands near an altar, adorned with garlands, on which rest two statuettes and a torch; on the right a column, adorned with bandages, supports an urn.

61. Oecus(3), wall E, section N: detail of the frieze of the blue epistyle, with fastened trefoils bordered at the bottom by a frame in which the motif of the leaves separated by hands is stylized. Above, a protruding coffered frame is represented.
63. Oecus(3), wall E, section N: detail of the middle area with the wooden column in which a rocchio with ashlar alternates with one with figures of offerers in relief.
62. Oecus (3), wall E, section N: detail of the black plinth with a slender vegetable candelabra consisting of a stem with a flower, between volute elements.
64. Oecus(3), E wall, N section: detail of the part above the red partition, with the tragic mask with a rich wreath of flowers, before the theft of 1982.
65. Oecus(3), wall E, section N: detail of the Corinthian capital, the wooden column and the frieze with the frame of leaves separated by hands, represented only as a contour line.
66. Oecus (3), wall E, central section: detail of the plinth in which only the left Siren of the two is preserved, ending in volutes and below the scaly columns.

67. Oecus(3), wall E, central section: on the podium of the plinth rest the bases with thin metal volutes of the columns with white and red scales that frame the open door towards an apsidal niche within which there is a female statue. On the crowning of the apse rest metal vases and shields that gain prominence on the black background of the tent hanging under the epistyle by means of red bandages. Behind run, in perspective, the two Ionic colonnades of the courtyard to which the scenographic wall is placed.

68. Oecus(3), wall E, central section: the open door reveals the slender female figure of a statue of a divinity (?) interpreted as Juno, due to the lack of particular characterizing attributes. AFS B303

69. Oecus(3), wall E, central section: detail of the Ionic colonnade visible on the left behind the black curtain fixed to rings. The frieze has a painted motif of buds between facing S-shaped volutes.

70. Oecus(3), wall E, central section: detail of the scaly column on the left, at the height of the architrave of the apse on which a globular vase and a shield rest. It can be seen how the scales are arranged according to axes with a parallel and not helical course, as in other cases.
71. Oecus(3), wallE, central section: detail of the metal amphora between two shields resting on the architrave of the apse.
72. Oecus(3), wall E, central section: detail of the circular lamp with bandages, suspended above the apse.
73. Oecus (3), wall E, central section: detail of the scaly column on the right and the metal amphora placed on the architrave of the apse, adorned with an acroterial palmette. 79 N53346

74. Oecus(3), wall E, central section: detail of the colonnade in perspective of the right side. On the frieze, also decorated with a bud between facing S-shaped volutes, runs an architrave with protruding platforms on which there are phallic meniscus.
75. Oecus(3), wall E, central section: detail of the frieze of the blue epistyle with fastened treflovers and corner column, surmounted by a protruding frame with square and rectangular coffers.
76. Oecus(3), wall E, section S: detail of the black plinth with a vegetable candelabra consisting of volute motifs and a stem with a bud.
77. Oecus(3),wall E, section S: detail of the virile herm, decorated with bandages, placed in the black plinth. The particular movement of the statue's face, turned to the left, is singular.
